title: Generate Lesson Analogies
description: Create memorable analogies that make complex concepts click for students.
prompt: Act as an expert educator with a knack for simplifying complex ideas. Create 5 creative and relatable analogies to explain [concept] to undergraduate students with no prior background in the subject. For each analogy: 1. Briefly describe the analogy. 2. Explain how it specifically relates to the target concept. 3. Identify one potential limitation or area where the analogy might break down to ensure student clarity.

title: Assessment Rubric Creator
description: Generate detailed rubrics for consistent and fair student evaluation.
prompt: You are an expert academic evaluator. Design a detailed rubric for evaluating [assignment type]. The rubric should include: 1. Specific evaluation criteria relevant to [assignment type]. 2. Four distinct performance levels (e.g., Exemplary, Proficient, Developing, Emerging). 3. Clear descriptors for each level/criteria intersection to ensure objective and consistent grading. Present the final rubric in a clear table format.

title: Literature Summary
description: Distil key findings from multiple research papers and surface gaps in the literature.
prompt: Act as a senior research analyst. Review the provided research papers on [topic] and provide a comprehensive summary. Structure your response as follows: 1. Executive Summary: A high-level overview of the current state of research. 2. Methodological Analysis: Compare the different methodologies used across the papers. 3. Key Findings: Synthesize common results and unique insights. 4. Research Gaps: Explicitly identify at least 3 areas where current research is lacking or where further investigation is needed. Cite specific papers wherever possible.

title: Research Question Generator
description: Generate novel, gap-filling research questions from an existing literature review.
prompt: Based on the provided literature review, act as a doctoral supervisor and suggest 5 novel, high-impact research questions. For each question: 1. State the question clearly. 2. Explain the specific research gap it addresses. 3. Briefly outline a potential methodological approach to answering it. 4. Identify the potential contribution to the field.

title: Meeting Agenda Draft
description: Generate a structured agenda with time allocations for any type of academic meeting.
prompt: Act as a highly organized administrative lead. Create a structured and goal-oriented meeting agenda for a [duration] meeting about [topic]. The agenda must include: 1. Clear meeting objectives. 2. A logical sequence of topics. 3. Specific time allocations for each topic. 4. Designated discussion points or desired outcomes for every item. 5. A 5-minute wrap-up section for action items and next steps.

title: Policy Summary
description: Condense complex policy documents into a clear one-page overview with action items.
prompt: You are a university compliance officer. Summarize the attached university policy document into a clear, one-page 'Action-Oriented Overview'. Your summary should include: 1. Purpose of the policy in 2-3 sentences. 2. Key requirements for [specific stakeholder group, e.g., faculty/students]. 3. A checklist of immediate action items. 4. Contact points for clarification. Use bullet points and bold text to highlight critical compliance requirements.

title: Case Study Framework
description: Build a structured, industry-specific case study for partner engagement and teaching.
prompt: Act as an industry-academic liaison. Develop a comprehensive case study framework for [industry/scenario] tailored for industry partner engagement. The framework should include sections for: 1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement. 2. Strategic Objectives. 3. Implementation Challenges & Solutions. 4. Quantitative and Qualitative Outcomes. 5. Key Lessons Learned. 6. Questions for Stakeholder Discussion. Ensure the tone is professional and showcases value-creation potential.

title: Simulation Scenario
description: Create immersive business scenarios that challenge student decision-making.
prompt: Create an immersive and realistic business simulation scenario for [domain] designed to test the decision-making skills of advanced learners. The scenario should: 1. Set the stage with a specific organizational context and a high-stakes challenge. 2. Provide 3-4 competing variables or constraints (e.g., budget, time, ethical considerations). 3. Present the user with 3 distinct possible courses of action. 4. Briefly describe the potential short-term and long-term consequences for each choice to facilitate follow-up reflection.

title: Learning Reflection
description: Structured weekly reflection guiding you to identify learning strengths and gaps.
prompt: Act as a growth-mindset coach. Guide me through a structured weekly learning reflection. Ask me the following questions one by one, waiting for my response after each: 1. What were your top 3 learning achievements this week? 2. What was the most significant challenge you faced, and how did you handle it? 3. Based on your progress, what are 2 specific areas you want to improve or focus on next week? 4. What is one practical step you can take on Monday to start that improvement? Finally, summarize our conversation into a brief 'Personal Growth Action Plan'.

title: Skill Gap Analysis
description: Diagnose skill gaps and get a personalized roadmap of learning resources to fill them.
prompt: You are a specialized career development consultant. Help me conduct a deep-dive skill gap analysis in [area]. 1. Ask me to list my current sub-skills and proficiency levels in this field. 2. Compare my input against industry standards for a [target role/level]. 3. Identify my top 3 critical gaps. 4. For each gap, recommend a mix of resources (e.g., one book/paper, one online course, and one practical project idea). Ensure the roadmap is progressive and actionable.
